Title: AKU-SONAM moving towards Curriculum Transformation
NewsSummary: The new curriculum will prepare future nurses and midwives for new challenges and leadership roles
NewsContent:
​

Ensuing the first theme of its new strategic plan for 2021 – 2026 ‘Transformation through Education’, AKU-SONAM has undertaken the initiative to revamp its curriculum in close coordination with the Quality, Teaching and L​​​​earning (QTL) network, office of the Provost. The move will help impart the most relevant knowledge to future nurses and midwives while preparing them to play a leadership role in our evolving global healthcare system. The new curriculum, which is currently undergoing transformation, will be at par with the top foreign nursing and midwifery universities.

The undergraduate curriculum committee outlined the steps to be taken for the systematic curriculum transformation. The changes in curriculum are guided by the expert Curriculum Advisors to ensure that it is not only internationally benchmarked but also locally relevant, while effectively incorporating digital technology tools and innovation. 

As a first step, the School carried out a stakeholder engagement survey to understand the existing gaps in the curriculum. The findings of the stakeholder mapping and the Peer Assessment Review (PAR) were used for redefining the Programme Learning Outcomes (PLOs). Additionally, the QTL network has been facilitating workshops for the faculty, teaching them how to revise the curriculum for maximum impact. 

“More than ever before, nurses and midwives need to be bold in their practice. We must work together to advocate for an equitable healthcare system that will be driven by nursing and midwifery leaders. Through Advanced Practice Nursing and a variety of multidisciplinary roles, we want to make a sizeable contribution to universal health targets. That’s where the transformational education comes in - our new outcome-based curriculum will train our students through innovative methods to address the most urgent healthcare, social and economic challenges of our time,” said Dr Rozina Karmaliani, Dean of AKU-SONAM.     

The outline for the outcome-based curriculum will be developed during the restructuring process. The School has initiated a series of faculty workshops to redesign teaching to competency-based education, using creative techniques and digital pedagogies, and moving toward authentic paperless exams and integrated assessments.  As a next step, the course learning outcomes will be realigned with the PLOs to match the AKU Graduate attributes and include essential competencies.​​  

Speaking about the curriculum transformation, Dr Khairulnissa Ajani, assistant dean, Teaching, Learning, and Undergraduate studies said, “At SONAM, we aim to be the trailblazers and become the most well-recognised university for nursing and midwifery education not just in Pakistan, but all over the world. As healthcare needs evolve, so should our education content. At SONAM, we believe in maintaining and surpassing the quality of academic and professional learning we offer to our students. The curriculum transformation will raise the bar of nursing in Pakistan.”
​
The future direction involves curriculum and course mapping followed by the revision of pedagogy and assessments. Once fully implemented, the outcome-based curriculum will lead to new collaboration opportunities with national leaders and top-ranking universities in the world.  ​
